summary: Master Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure, boiling point elevation calculations, and thermodynamic K_b derivations.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure (RLVP)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure (RLVP)

summaryBox.title: RLVP Formula
summaryBox.takeaway: Δp / p°_A = x_B. For dilute solutions: Δp / p°_A ≈ n_B / n_A = (w_B M_A) / (M_B w_A).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
RELATIVE LOWERING OF VAPOR PRESSURE (RLVP)

(p°_A - p_A) / p°_A = Δp / p°_A = x_B = n_B / (n_A + n_B)

For dilute solutions (n_B ≪ n_A):
Δp / p°_A ≈ n_B / n_A = (w_B × M_A) / (M_B × w_A)
conceptBreakdown.content: Non-volatile solute molecules occupy surface sites on the liquid, lowering the rate of vaporization. The relative lowering of vapor pressure ($\Delta p / p_A^\circ$) equals the **mole fraction of solute ($x_B$)**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Boiling Point Elevation (ΔT_b) & K_b Derivation
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Boiling Point Elevation (ΔT_b) & K_b Derivation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
BOILING POINT ELEVATION (ΔT_b)

ΔT_b = T_b - T°_b = K_b × m = K_b × (w_B × 1000) / (M_B × w_A in g)

Thermodynamic Formula for K_b:
K_b = (R × M_A × (T°_b)²) / (1000 × Δ_vap H)
Units of K_b: K·kg/mol (depends strictly on SOLVENT, independent of solute)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Boiling Point Elevation**: $\mathbf{\Delta T_b = K_b \cdot m}$ where $K_b$ is the Ebullioscopic Constant ($\text{K}\cdot\text{kg/mol}$).
• **Thermodynamic Relation**: $K_b$ depends strictly on solvent properties ($M_A, T_b^\circ, \Delta_{\text{vap}} H$), and is completely independent of the solute's chemical identity.

quickRevision: RLVP equals the mole fraction of solute (x_B).
K_b depends strictly on the solvent, not the solute.
keyFormulae: \Delta T_b = K_b \cdot m, \quad K_b = \frac{R \cdot M_A \cdot (T_b^\circ)^2}{1000 \cdot \Delta_{\text{vap}} H}
